Hello Freya,

I have finished the notes for Saturday's repair cafe. The room booking covers the morning session and the time we need to clear up, so nobody has to rush out while a visitor is still packing a bag. The caretaker will unlock the side door at eight. Please ask volunteers to use that entrance until the main doors open, as the floor by reception will still be wet. The first table on the left is for registration. It needs a paper list, a few pencils and the box of numbered cards. The list uses invented names in the training copy, and the contact address printed at the top is repair-desk@example.com. We should put that copy away before visitors arrive. The second table is for small sewing jobs. There is a lamp with a magnifying lens, a tin of bobbins and a packet of new needles. The machine has already been checked. Its foot pedal belongs in the padded bag when we move it, even for a short distance. The small trolley can carry the machine and lamp together, provided the lead is tied loosely around the handle. A tight knot would be awkward to undo and might damage the cable. Behind the table, leave enough space for someone to sit with a walking frame beside the chair. We can move the spare stools into the store if the aisle feels cramped. Please keep the low chair with arms near the entrance for anyone who needs to rest while waiting. It is not a place for coats or boxes. The hooks by the window are available for those.

For the electrical bench, I have asked each volunteer to work only within their own experience. The event is a place to examine ordinary household objects, explain what we can see and sometimes make a simple repair. A visitor may leave with advice rather than a working object. Our registration card says this plainly. We must also record when we decline a job, including a brief reason, so that the next person does not mistake an unfinished check for an approval. The sample card reads "Not tested" in large letters. Please keep the word "Not" visible when you lay the cards out. The green stickers are for the storage boxes and do not indicate a successful test. The portable appliance tester has its own log, which the trained volunteer will complete. Nobody else needs to enter figures there. We have no arrangement to retain a visitor's computer overnight, and we should not offer to copy a disk as a favour during a busy session. If an object needs a specialist or spare parts that we cannot identify, we can explain that and let the owner decide what to do next. The printed directory contains only public workshop details. The demonstration sheet, on the other hand, uses a reserved hostname, workshop.invalid, and should remain with the teaching materials. Its mock ticket says "recieved at desk" because we are showing how an old form looked. That quoted label should remain exactly as it is. The new blank forms use the standard spelling. There is also a sample filename, `reciept_scan.txt`, in the handout. It is an identifier for an exercise, so please do not silently rename it when making copies.

The cafe team will put tea, decaf coffee and water on the round table. We have oat drink as well as milk, and the biscuits will stay in their original packets so that guests can read the ingredient lists. The treasurer has left a cash float in a sealed envelope. Donations go in the separate tin, and nobody needs to explain or justify the amount they choose to give. We are keeping the donation sign small because the main purpose of the morning is the work at the tables. At lunchtime, the last volunteer at each bench should collect loose screws, check beneath the chairs and wipe the tabletop. Put any unidentified part in a clear bag with the table number on it. Do not put it in the mixed box and hope someone recognises it next month. We have agreed that the registration sheets remain with the organiser, while the anonymous count of completed, declined and unfinished jobs goes into the meeting notes. These are different records. A finished job does not automatically mean a saved object, since the owner may still choose to replace it. For the newsletter, I would prefer a plain account of what happened to a claim about waste that we cannot measure. We can say how many people came, how many objects reached a bench and how many volunteers helped. The photographer will ask before taking a close picture and can use the empty room for general shots. Finally, please leave the linen tea towels hanging over the rack rather than folded in a damp heap. I will take them home after the room check. The caretaker's checklist is on the noticeboard by the exit, and I can stay until the last item has been signed off.

Thanks,
Noor Ashby
Volunteer coordinator
